title: Bipedal3 element with paper bitwise formulas + proptest tests
description:
Implement `Bipedal3` (a single-`u64`-pair value packing 64 $\mathbb{F}_3$ elements) with the paper's bitwise add / sub / mul / neg formulas and proptest cross-checks against the scalar reference.

## Background

Theorem 2.1 of the reference paper gives bitwise formulas for $\mathbb{F}_3$ ops on the 4-state $(mag, sgn)$ representation: `mul = (m1 & m2, s1 ^ s2)` (2 ops); `add` and `sub` use 6 ops each with CSE. This issue lands a `Bipedal3` type at `gf2-algebra::packed::bipedal3` whose semantics match those formulas exactly, with proptest cross-checks against `ScalarPackedFp3` (T2) on every lane index.

Per the D1b approval, `Eq` is canonical-decode equality so the alternative-zero codeword `(mag=0, sgn=1)` compares equal to canonical zero. `lane(i)` canonicalises; `with_lane` only ever writes the canonical encoding; `all_zero` is true for both alt-zero and canonical zero.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `Bipedal3` packs exactly 64 $\mathbb{F}_3$ elements into two `u64`s (mag and sgn) and implements `PackedField<Fp<3>>`.
- [ ] [hard] `add`, `sub`, `mul`, `neg` use the bitwise formulas from the paper's Theorem 2.1; the implementation is a direct transliteration with CSE.
- [ ] [hard] Proptest cross-checks `add`, `sub`, `mul`, `neg` against `ScalarPackedFp3` on 1000 random pairs; the alternative-zero codeword is included in the input distribution.
- [ ] [hard] Lane semantics: `lane(i)` canonicalises the alt-zero codeword to `Fp<3>::ZERO`; `with_lane` writes only canonical encoding; `Eq` compares decoded values so alt-zero == canonical zero.
- [ ] [hard] `cargo nextest run -p gf2-algebra --release --profile ci` passes.
